content.text: 23Thierno is an emerging Dominican urban artist, born in 2001 in San Cristóbal, whose catalogue on the streaming platforms begins in 2024.
Releases

The earliest of his releases on Apple Music, «Panas Falsos» and «With “U”», date from 2024, along with «Love It», made with Yauri GM, and «No Me Haces Falta», made with Johcrap Marfer. In 2025 came «Monotonía», «Mi Cocola» with FlowYeraldy and «Baby You», a track credited to Angel Fire, 23Thierno and Johcrap Marfer that has an official video on his YouTube channel. He is also the featured artist on «Le Jure» by Angi Fire and DJ Human Star, and his most recent single, «Nena», is dated 27 February 2026.
Legacy
His work is recent and documented mainly on the platforms where it is released.

Abigail Vásquez is a Dominican Christian singer and worship leader celebrated for her passionate vocal interpretations and healing-centered devotional music.
Origins and musical calling

Born in Santo Domingo, Vásquez grew up immersed in the spiritual life and choral assemblies of the local evangelical church. Her early musical development centered on congregational worship, fostering a heartfelt style focused on divine grace and biblical promise.
Impact of «Te Tocaré» and discography

Vásquez achieved international reach with the release of «Te Tocaré», an emotive worship ballad inspired by biblical accounts of faith and physical restoration. The song circulated across digital streaming services and YouTube, solidifying her voice within modern Christian hymnody alongside titles like «Tu Gracia» and «Rindo Mi Corazón».
Live ministry and spiritual vision

Her performances blend contemporary acoustic praise with passionate vocal climaxes designed for congregational engagement. Through live conferences, media outreach, and worship recordings, Vásquez continually directs audiences toward deeper spiritual communion.
Abigail Vásquez is a Dominican Christian singer whose publicly documented videos center on worship music. Her own channel records performances from 2020 through 2026.
Recorded performances
In a 2020 video she presented «Amor Sin Condición» as a cover. Another video from 2024 presents «Alma Mía» as a cover. Both document her interpretations of existing songs.
Live sessions
Her channel later posted worship medleys and live sessions, including «Te Tocaré (Live Session)» in 2026.
Legacy
Her video record documents a continuing worship repertoire across cover performances and later live sessions.

content.text: Abigail Vásquez es una cantante y salmista cristiana dominicana distinguida por su capacidad interpretativa y su repertorio de alabanza congregacional.
Orígenes y vocación ministerial

Nacida en Santo Domingo, creció vinculada a la liturgia comunitaria y a los ministerios corales de las iglesias cristianas de la capital. Desde sus primeros años consagró su voz al servicio eclesiástico, perfilando un estilo devocional de marcado arraigo escritural.
Trascendencia de «Te Tocaré» y discografía

Cobró notoriedad en el circuito de música de fe con el lanzamiento de «Te Tocaré», cántico fundamentado en los pasajes bíblicos de sanidad y fe perseverante que circuló en plataformas digitales. Su discografía incluye además temas destacados como «Tu Gracia» y «Rindo Mi Corazón».
Ministerio en vivo y visión espiritual

La instrumentación de sus canciones combina elementos de la balada acústica y el pop contemporáneo con una sobria entrega vocal. Abigail Vásquez participa activamente en jornadas de adoración, campañas evangelísticas y retiros espirituales en toda la geografía dominicana.
Abigail Vásquez es una cantante cristiana dominicana cuyos videos documentados se centran en la música de adoración. En su propio canal aparecen interpretaciones publicadas entre 2020 y 2026.
Interpretaciones grabadas

En un video de 2020 presentó «Amor Sin Condición» como versión de otro tema. Otro video, de 2024, identifica «Alma Mía» también como versión. Ambos documentan sus interpretaciones de canciones ajenas.
Sesiones en vivo
Más adelante publicó popurrís de adoración y sesiones en vivo en su canal, entre ellas «Te Tocaré (Live Session)» en 2026.
Legado
Sus videos permiten seguir un repertorio de adoración que va de las versiones de otros temas a las sesiones en vivo posteriores.

content.text: Ada Betsabé (Santo Domingo, 29 January 1991) is a Dominican rapper, songwriter and producer who works in Spanish and English at once. She has released everything through her own label since 2015 and describes herself as a minister as readily as an artist.
Early years and formation

She left Santo Domingo at four, when her parents emigrated, and grew up between New York City and Massachusetts. She has worked out of Worcester since. She was thirteen when a cousin dared her to write a rap; it became her way of getting things out, and the writing has stayed at the centre of the work.
Nuevopact Records and first recordings
In 2015, at twenty-four, she founded her own label, Nuevopact Records, and opened it with Freedom. Everything she has released since has come out through it.

Mi Escudo reached furthest of the early records and is now a decade old; Santo, Alive, Vengan and the English-language Sparrow belong to the same stretch. The Personal EP followed in 2018 — Emotional, Corazón, Tu Nombre, God Body, and Suficiente with Sueezy. That same year she released Trapstorno (Versión Femenina), answering
’s record from a woman’s side, and appeared on Madiel Lara’s Uno Cinco with Arias FTW and Niko Eme.
Expansion of genres
Masterpiece arrived in 2020, carrying La Vía, 4:13 and Apunta with

. Alarma came in 2022 and moved her into drill: she produced it herself with Jalapeño Beats, wrote it and performed it, and the video was shot in San Francisco under the direction of Dennis Guillen. ¿Ahora Qué? and Solita sit alongside it in trap.
El Fin Se Acerca and recent work
Trono, with CH Gedeones, came around 2023. She cut Pecado with
, Intervención with Tbabz, No Se Va with
, and Súbele with Rambo Cristiano in September 2025, and she appears on Alguien Como Tú alongside
and
. The EP El Fin Se Acerca arrived in September 2025, opening with Inmortal. A new run of songs followed in 2026.
Style: Spanglish

She raps in Spanish and in English, often inside the same song, and the records are labelled accordingly: Sin Límites went out as a Spanglish Remix, Lottery as Spanglish Trap, Cuenta – Blessings as a Spanglish Cover. English tracks like Sparrow, Alive and The Cure sit in the same catalogue as Mi Escudo, Santo and De Rodillas, and neither side is a translation of the other. Asked to name her language, she writes Spanglish.
Ministry and media
She posts about discipleship as often as about releases — making disciples rather than fans, in her own phrase. Alongside the music she works with the outlet Real Vida TV.

Adalgisa Pantaleón is a Dominican singer, actress and writer born on November 10, 1954 in San Francisco de Macorís. Her career spans multiple genres—merengue, bachata, tropical, and bolero—and extends across performance, recording, and written work. Between the mid-1980s and the 2010s, she recorded prolifically, building a presence across Dominican music and entertainment culture that reflects the breadth of her artistic range.
Career and recording

Pantaleón's earliest documented album is El Hombre & Su Musica from 1985, marking the beginning of a career that would span nearly three decades and produce over twenty recorded works. Her recordings span multiple labels and styles, reflecting the adaptability and reach of her artistry. Among her notable releases are albums from the late 1980s and 1990s, including collaborations that positioned her within the broader landscape of Dominican music.
In 1988, she appeared on the album Wilfrido... El Baile, working alongside

, one of the country's most commercially successful bandleaders. That collaboration speaks to her standing within the professional recording world. Throughout the 1990s and 2000s, her discography continued to expand with titles including Veneno Para El Corazón (1993), Fogará! (1994), Ventana Abierta (1995), Mas Ternura (1997), and Ni Es Lo Mismo Ni Es Igual (1998), each marking her presence in the recording industry.
Multiple artistic identities

What distinguishes Pantaleón from many of her contemporaries is the multiplicity of her professional identities. Beyond recording, she has worked as an actress and as a writer, engaging with Dominican culture through different media. This breadth is unusual in a music industry that tends to specialize, and it positions her within a smaller cohort of artists who sustained careers across multiple forms.

Her later recordings—La Llave De Mi Corazón (2007) and Asondeguerra (2011)—extend her documented activity into the 2010s, testament to her sustained engagement with recording and performance long into her later years.
Legacy

Pantaleón belongs to the generation of Dominican recording artists who built their careers through the CD era and maintained them as formats and technologies changed. Her work across genres and media reflects an approach to artistic practice in which the boundaries between music, theater and written expression are fluid. Her recording career, preserved in Discogs and other music databases, documents the actual work of a professional musician across a period of significant change in Dominican music.

Adalgisa Pantaleón, born Ramona Adalgisa Pantaleón Fernández on November 10, 1954, in San Francisco de Macorís, is a Dominican singer, actress and writer. She emerged at the 1971 «Festival de la Voz», spent more than two decades singing with «4.40» led by
, and released her first solo CD, «Al son del sol», in 2003.
Early years and first stage appearances
Pantaleón grew up singing with her mother and in school and church choirs in San Francisco de Macorís. At sixteen she represented the city in the 1971 «Festival de la Voz», organized by
, and placed third. Solano then supported her first professional appearances; her solo career was already under way before she joined «4.40».
Years with «4.40»
She joined

's «4.40» in 1989 and remained one of its singers for more than two decades. Her voice is heard on «Como abeja al panal», from «Bachata Rosa» (1990). These were group recordings and performances, a major part of her career but distinct from albums released under her own name.
Her solo album and later recordings
In 2003 Pantaleón presented «Al son del sol», described by contemporary Dominican press as her first solo CD. Produced by
for «Infovox», the album moves among son, bolero and other Caribbean rhythms. It includes «Qué sería de mí», written for her by
. In 2026 she and
presented the music video for «La receta perfecta», a bachata he wrote and included on his album «El saborcito de tu amor».
Writing, acting and recognition

Pantaleón published the poetry collection «Mi silencio roto» in 1995. She played María in the 1997 film «Nueba Yol III: Bajo la nueva ley» and received a 1998 «Premio ACE» for her performance. Her work has also included television and theatre. In 2023 the Dominican government awarded her the «Medalla al Mérito de la Mujer Dominicana» in the cultural and artistic category.
Legacy

Her documented career extends from the Dominican singing contests of the early 1970s to the international repertoire of «4.40», a solo album rooted in Caribbean music, and work in literature and film. The 2023 national award recognized that sustained contribution across artistic forms.

Adalgisa Pantaleón es una cantante, actriz y escritora dominicana nacida el 10 de noviembre de 1954 en San Francisco de Macorís. Su carrera abarca múltiples géneros—merengue, bachata, tropical y bolero—y se extiende a través de la actuación, la grabación y el trabajo literario. Entre mediados de los años ochenta y los años diez, grabó prolíficamente, construyendo una presencia en la música y la cultura de entretenimiento dominicanas que refleja la amplitud de su rango artístico.
Carrera y grabación

El álbum documentado más temprano de Pantaleón es El Hombre & Su Musica de 1985, marcando el comienzo de una carrera que se extendería casi tres décadas y produciría más de veinte obras grabadas. Sus grabaciones abarcan múltiples sellos y estilos, reflejando la adaptabilidad y alcance de su artistry. Entre sus lanzamientos notables se encuentran álbumes de finales de los años ochenta y noventa, incluyendo colaboraciones que la posicionaron dentro del panorama más amplio de la música dominicana.
En 1988, apareció en el álbum Wilfrido... El Baile, trabajando junto a

, uno de los directores de banda más exitosos comercialmente del país. Esa colaboración habla de su posición dentro del mundo profesional de grabación. A lo largo de los años noventa y dos mil, su discografía continuó expandiéndose con títulos como Veneno Para El Corazón (1993), Fogará! (1994), Ventana Abierta (1995), Mas Ternura (1997) y Ni Es Lo Mismo Ni Es Igual (1998), cada uno marcando su presencia en la industria de grabación.
Múltiples identidades artísticas

Lo que distingue a Pantaleón de muchas de sus contemporáneas es la multiplicidad de sus identidades profesionales. Más allá de la grabación, ha trabajado como actriz y como escritora, comprometiéndose con la cultura dominicana a través de diferentes medios. Esta amplitud es inusual en una industria musical que tiende a especializarse, y la posiciona dentro de un cohorte más pequeño de artistas que sustentaron carreras a través de múltiples formas.

Sus grabaciones posteriores—La Llave De Mi Corazón (2007) y Asondeguerra (2011)—extienden su actividad documentada hacia los años diez, testimonio de su compromiso sostenido con la grabación y la actuación mucho en sus años posteriores.
Legado

Pantaleón pertenece a la generación de artistas grabadores dominicanos que construyeron sus carreras a través de la era del CD y las mantuvieron mientras los formatos y tecnologías cambiaban. Su obra a través de géneros y medios refleja un enfoque de la práctica artística en el cual los límites entre la música, el teatro y la expresión escrita son fluidos. Su carrera de grabación, preservada en Discogs y otras bases de datos de música, documenta el trabajo real de una músico profesional a lo largo de un período de cambio significativo en la música dominicana.

Adalgisa Pantaleón, nombre artístico de Ramona Adalgisa Pantaleón Fernández, es una cantante, actriz y escritora dominicana nacida el 10 de noviembre de 1954 en San Francisco de Macorís. Se dio a conocer en el «Festival de la Voz» de 1971, fue una de las voces de «4.40» durante más de dos décadas y publicó su primer CD solista, «Al son del sol», en 2003.
Primeros años y primeros escenarios

En su infancia cantó con su madre y participó en coros escolares y religiosos de San Francisco de Macorís. A los dieciséis años representó a su ciudad en el «Festival de la Voz» de 1971, organizado por
, donde obtuvo el tercer lugar. El maestro la acompañó en sus primeras presentaciones profesionales. Para cuando ingresó a «4.40», Pantaleón ya había desarrollado una carrera como solista.
La etapa en «4.40»
En 1989 se incorporó a «4.40», la agrupación de

, y permaneció en ella por más de veinte años. Su voz forma parte de «Como abeja al panal», incluida en «Bachata Rosa» (1990). Esa discografía pertenece al grupo y a Guerra; las grabaciones dan cuenta de su trabajo como integrante, distinto de sus lanzamientos a nombre propio.
Un disco propio y nuevas colaboraciones
En 2003 presentó «Al son del sol», señalado por la prensa de la época como su primer CD solista.
produjo el álbum para el sello «Infovox», con un repertorio que recorre el son, el bolero y otros ritmos caribeños.
compuso para ella «Qué sería de mí», una de sus canciones. En 2026 presentó con
el videoclip de «La receta perfecta», bachata escrita por él e incluida en su álbum «El saborcito de tu amor».
Escritura, cine y reconocimiento

Además del canto, publicó el poemario «Mi silencio roto» en 1995. Interpretó a María en la película «Nueba Yol III: Bajo la nueva ley» (1997), trabajo por el que recibió un «Premio ACE» en 1998. También ha actuado en televisión y teatro. En 2023 recibió la «Medalla al Mérito de la Mujer Dominicana» en el renglón cultural y artístico.
Legado

La trayectoria de Pantaleón une el circuito de festivales de los años setenta, una prolongada labor vocal en «4.40», su propio álbum de ritmos caribeños y obras de literatura y cine. La distinción estatal de 2023 reconoció esa continuidad entre distintas formas de expresión artística.

Sounds

content.text: Adriana Green is a prominent Dominican singer, psalmist, and radio host who achieved international recognition as the winner of the second season of The Voice Dominicana in October 2022. Her artistic profile blends a long career in commercial tropical and romantic music with a deep ministry as a Christian worship leader and community advocate.
Early Life and Musical Beginnings
Birth and Childhood
She was born on January 1, 1981, in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, but was raised from infancy by her paternal grandparents in the city of La Romana.
Discovery of Her Talent

At age 17, while organizing a choir for her high school graduation, a backing musician noticed her incredible vocal potential. He assured her she had a future in singing and offered her her first formal job.
Commercial Career

She began her professional career singing in a guitar trio at Casa de Campo and later performed at local piano bars. In parallel, she worked for 10 years as a radio host and commercial voiceover artist for prominent local stations like Ritmo 96, Mambo 94.9 FM, and Amor FM.
Conversion and Ministry (Psalmist)

At age 24, she experienced a radical life change by converting to Christianity. From that moment on, she redirected her interpretive talent and began developing her role as a psalmist, dedicating her voice to worship and sharing messages of faith.During the global COVID-19 pandemic, she became widely known in her home region for launching spontaneous tours through the neighborhoods of La Romana, singing from the streets to bring comfort to citizens. Additionally, she founded and directs the Panes y Peces (Loaves and Fishes) Foundation, a community organization focused on helping underprivileged families.
Victory on The Voice Dominicana
After a hiatus from commercial stages, Adriana decided to audition for the famous singing competition. She joined the team of legendary merengue artist

(Team Milly). On October 23, 2022, after dazzling the judges and the public with memorable performances like "Yo viviré" (I Will Survive), she was crowned the winner of the grand finale, securing a trophy, a cash prize, and an international record deal.

A 2013 profile documented Green's work as a Christian singer. Her connection to La Romana is biographical rather than a claim about where she was born: she grew up there and identifies with the province.

content.text: Adriana Green es una destacada cantante, salmista y locutora de radio dominicana que alcanzó el reconocimiento internacional tras coronarse como ganadora de la segunda temporada de The Voice Dominicana en octubre de 2022. Su perfil artístico combina una extensa trayectoria en la música comercial tropical y romántica con un profundo ministerio como líder de adoración cristiana y defensora comunitaria.
Primeros años y comienzos musicales
Nacimiento e infancia
Nació el 1 de enero de 1981 en Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, pero desde su infancia fue criada por sus abuelos paternos en la ciudad de La Romana.
Descubrimiento de su talento

A los 17 años, mientras organizaba un coro para su graduación de la escuela secundaria, un músico de acompañamiento notó su increíble potencial vocal. Él le aseguró que tenía un gran futuro en el canto y le ofreció su primer trabajo formal.
Carrera comercial

Comenzó su trayectoria profesional cantando en un trío de guitarras en Casa de Campo y, más tarde, se presentó en diversos piano bars locales. En paralelo, trabajó durante 10 años como locutora de radio y artista de locución comercial para destacadas emisoras locales como Ritmo 96, Mambo 94.9 FM y Amor FM.
Conversión y ministerio (Salmista)

A los 24 años, experimentó un cambio radical de vida al convertirse al cristianismo. A partir de ese momento, redirigió su talento interpretativo y comenzó a desarrollar su rol como salmista, dedicando su voz a la adoración y a compartir mensajes de fe.

Durante la pandemia global de COVID-19, se dio a conocer ampliamente en su región natal por realizar recorridos espontáneos por los barrios de La Romana, cantando desde las calles para llevar consuelo a los ciudadanos. Además, fundó y dirige la Fundación Panes y Peces, una organización comunitaria enfocada en ayudar a familias de escasos recursos.
Victoria en The Voice Dominicana
Tras un paréntesis fuera de los escenarios comerciales, Adriana decidió audicionar para la famosa competencia de canto. Se integró al equipo de la legendaria artista de merengue

(Team Milly). El 23 de octubre de 2022, luego de deslumbrar a los jueces y al público con interpretaciones memorables como "Yo viviré" (I Will Survive), se coronó ganadora de la gran final, asegurando un trofeo, un premio en efectivo y un contrato discográfico internacional.

content.text: Adriel Music is an emerging Dominican urban artist who began writing songs in New York as a young teenager and has released his music from Santo Domingo.
Style

According to a 2021 press note, he had tried trap and dembow before settling on a fusion of styles that leans on his range, his flow and danceable rhythms, and which he says is what audiences demand at parties and clubs.
Releases

His single «La calle ta prendía», released in May 2021, was presented as a dance track for a public who wanted to enjoy themselves again after the pandemic; its video is on his YouTube channel. The channel also carries the official video of «Desde Abajo», credited with Mario TSB.
Legacy
His work is recent and documented mainly by his channel and by the press note on «La calle ta prendía».

Adriel Music is a Dominican urban-music singer whose documented releases span 2021 to 2023. His early public account places the beginning of his songwriting in New York City, without establishing his birthplace.
Early work

A 2021 press profile reported that Adriel was writing songs informally in New York at age thirteen. He explored trap and dembow before turning to a blend of urban styles. In April 2021 he promoted «La calle ta' prendía», accompanied by a video on his own channel.
Recorded singles

His later digital releases include «La Combi» and «Desde Abajo» in 2022, followed by «Modo Joseo» and «Tu No Mete Na» in 2023. These dated recordings extend the record of his work beyond the single discussed in the 2021 press profile.

The documented sequence from «La calle ta' prendía» through the 2023 singles shows a continued recording career across several forms of Dominican urban music.

Estilo

Según una nota de prensa de 2021, había probado el trap y el dembow antes de quedarse con una fusión de estilos que se apoya en su registro, su manera de frasear y unos ritmos bailables, y que según él es lo que reclama el público en fiestas y discotecas.
Lanzamientos

Su sencillo «La calle ta prendía», de mayo de 2021, se presentó como un tema para bailar dirigido a un público que quería volver a divertirse después de la pandemia; su video está en su canal de YouTube. El canal incluye también el video oficial de «Desde Abajo», acreditado con Mario TSB.
Legado
Su obra es reciente y está documentada sobre todo en su canal y en la nota de prensa sobre «La calle ta prendía».

Comienzos

content.text: Agapito Pascual (born 24 June 1962), who bills himself as A lo Moderno, is a Dominican merengue típico accordionist, singer and composer. He came to the accordion the long way round — he was a tambora player first, and a good enough one as a teenager to be hired by the biggest names in the genre before he ever led anything of his own.
Early years and formation

He was born in La Balsa de La Isabela, in Puerto Plata, into a very poor family, and was working by the age of seven — in the fields and shining shoes. He started playing at seven as well, on the drum, and was good enough young enough that the musicians around him took notice. Six brothers in the family became musicians.
On tambora
By 1978 and 1979 he was being sought out by the established típico bands, playing for
, for
, and for Bartolo Alvarado — the accordionist the country knows as
. Backing three bandleaders of that rank before turning twenty is an apprenticeship rather than a job, and it is where he learned the music from inside the rhythm section.
From drum to accordion

He then taught himself the accordion, which in merengue típico is the lead instrument and the one the group is named after, and formed his own conjunto in 1987. Moving from the back line to the front of a típico group is not a common route; most accordionists start on the accordion. He passed the instrument on: his sister
, who leads her own conjunto in New York as La Mami del Swing, learned it from him.
Mangú Records

He signed with Mangú Records in November 1997 and made three albums for the label: El Café en Pilón that same year, Muchachita Linda in November 1998, and El Mamón in 2000, cut at the Audio Enfi studios in Santiago. La Mujer Moderna, El Paquetazo de Mujeres and La Hija de La Vecina belong to the same body of work.

La Vieja y Su Pipa, El Café en Pilón, La Mujer Moderna, La Pobre Adela, La Moderna Agarradera, Lejos de Mí and El Joven Moderno are the ones that stayed in circulation. The titles run to the comic and the everyday, which is where típico has always done its best work.
Frente a Frente
Frente a Frente: Dos Estrellas en Uno pairs him against

across a single record — the head-to-head format típico has long used to put two accordionists in the same room. The man he had drummed behind two decades earlier was now on the other side of the billing.
A lo Moderno

The tag is his own and he uses it everywhere: on the records, in the song titles, as the name of his page. He works out of Miami now, and he has not stopped — El Palo Prendío came out in 2026, close to forty years after he first stood in front of his own conjunto. He and Fidelina still play together.

Agapito Pascual (nacido el 24 de junio de 1962), que se anuncia como A lo Moderno, es un acordeonista, cantante y compositor de merengue típico dominicano. Al acordeón llegó por el camino largo: primero fue tamborero, y lo bastante bueno de adolescente como para que lo buscaran los nombres grandes del género antes de dirigir nada suyo.
Primeros años y formación

Nació en La Balsa de La Isabela, en Puerto Plata, en una familia muy humilde, y a los siete años ya trabajaba: en la agricultura y limpiando zapatos. A los siete también empezó a tocar, en el tambor, y lo hacía bastante bien y bastante temprano como para que los músicos del entorno se fijaran en él. Seis hermanos de la familia salieron músicos.
Tamborero
Para 1978 y 1979 lo buscaban los conjuntos típicos establecidos: tocó con
, con
y con Bartolo Alvarado, el acordeonista que el país conoce como
. Acompañar a tres directores de ese calibre antes de los veinte es un aprendizaje antes que un empleo, y es donde aprendió la música desde dentro de la sección rítmica.
Del tambor al acordeón

Después aprendió acordeón —que en el merengue típico es el instrumento líder y el que le da nombre al conjunto— y montó el suyo en 1987. Pasar de la parte de atrás al frente de un conjunto típico no es ruta común; casi todos los acordeonistas empiezan en el acordeón. El instrumento lo pasó adelante: su hermana

Aguakate is a Dominican merengue típico group formed in New York in 2003 around the singer Gerpis Correa, known as

Formation

Music directories say the group was created by José Mateo Peligro together with Correa, on the label Peligro Records. The name comes from a word Correa used constantly to say that everything was fine; the producer took it as a proposal for the band. The early lineup listed accordionist Belarminio Liriano, Pedro Lantigua on congas, Waldi on guitar, Alejandro on bass, DJ Chucky on piano, Diógenes on saxophone, Fermín Flores on backing vocals and Eddie on percussion.
Records

In 2004 the group signed with Universal Latino and released its debut «De otra galaxia», a twelve-track album that includes «La gallinita», «Mueva esa vaina», «La agarradera», «El divorcio», «Solo con un beso» and «Reggaeton ripiao». In March 2004 came the live album «En vivo desde Santo Domingo», and the same year «Aguakate vs Krisspy: mano a mano», with
, on Mambo Records. «Crazyssimo» followed in August 2006 with «Tu pussycat» and «La conquista», recorded with

. A 2015 release of «Pussy Cat» credits Aguakate alongside
and Mala Fe.
Split and return

The group broke up in 2006 when Correa began a solo project as Shino Aguakate with the producer Frasier Hernández, who encouraged him to combine styles. It returned in 2010 with Correa as leader and shareholder, most of the former musicians back and management by M&M Enterprises. It has toured Jamaica, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico, Alaska, Canada and several US cities, and in June 2011 played the Puerto Rican Festival organized by the station La Mega 97.9 at 112th Street and Third Avenue in Manhattan, with «El amor que perdimos», «Danza kuduro» and «Aléjate de mí».
Style

The band played fast merengue típico with rapid instrumental solos and mixed it with romantic merengue, reggaeton and urban rhythms. In «Reggaeton ripiao» the rhythm changes from merengue to a reggaeton pattern adapted for the tambora, a mixture that was controversial among típico purists.
Legacy
Aguakate is documented through its albums with Universal and the later career of Correa, who continues under the name Shino Aguakate.
